title: New Every Morning
subtitle: Lamentations in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
Lamentations is a book of tears for a fallen city. Jerusalem sits alone like a widow. The roads to Zion are empty, the gates have sunk into the ground, the gold has grown dim, and a fox walks across the holy mountain. And at the very center of the book, in the dark, a poet remembers something, and says it out loud: his mercies are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.

This book walks through it in thirty short poems, in five parts, one for each chapter of the old lament. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with what the city left behind—a lamp burning low, an ember in the ash, a lyre lying in the dust—and leave the faces to your imagination. If you are grieving, you are welcome here, and you don't have to hurry to the hopeful part.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the book of Lamentations alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

paintings.title: how
paintings.epigraph: “How the city sits solitary, that was full of people!”
paintings.poem:
the market stalls are standing.
the doors are standing.
the well still has its rope.

only the people
are gone.

that is how the book begins.
not with a reason,
not with a lesson,
just a long look
down an empty street

and one small word
that is almost a cry:

how.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “how” (Lamentations 1:1) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“not with a reason, not with a lesson, just a long look down an empty street and one small word that is almost a cry: how”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
市场摊位矗立着。
门是竖着的。
井里还有绳子。

只有人民
消失了。

这就是本书的开头。
没有理由，
不带教训，
只是长看一眼
沿着一条空荡荡的街道

和一个小字
这几乎是一声哭喊：

怎么样。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天早上你走出的门旁挂着今天的“如何”（耶利米哀歌 1：1）的画，那么它的最后一行——“没有理由，没有教训，只是长时间地看着一条空荡荡的街道，一个几乎是哭泣的小词：如何”——会如何影响你的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “这座城市多么孤独，却挤满了人！”

paintings.title: in the night
paintings.epigraph: “She weeps bitterly in the night. Her tears are on her cheeks.”
paintings.poem:
the day has chores in it.
bread, water, the door, the fire.

it's at night
that grief sits up.

she weeps in the night,
the poem says,
and her tears are on her cheeks,

not wiped away yet,
not explained,
just there
where anyone who came close
could see them.

if that is you tonight,
you are in good company.
you are not the first
to cry in the dark
and be written down
in the Bible.10
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (Lamentations 1:2)—where in your own home or work today does “you are not the first to cry in the dark and be written down in the Bible.10” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
这一天有家务活。
面包、水、门、火。

现在是晚上
悲伤坐了起来。

她在夜里哭泣，
这首诗说，
她的泪水挂在脸颊上，

还没有抹掉，
没有解释，
就在那里
任何靠近的人
可以看到他们。

如果今晚是你的话
你们有很好的伙伴。
你不是第一个
在黑暗中哭泣
并被写下来
圣经中.10
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路历程中的每一站都展示了神如何在平凡的地方与我们相遇（耶利米哀歌 1:2）——今天在你自己的家里或工作场所，“你不是第一个在黑暗中哭泣并被记录在《圣经》中的人。10”听起来是真的吗？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “她在夜里哭得很伤心。她的泪水挂在脸颊上。”

paintings.title: the roads mourn
paintings.epigraph: “The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to the solemn assembly.”
paintings.poem:
no feet on them now.
no singing up the hill
at festival time,
no children running ahead.

grass in the wheel ruts.
a lizard on a warm stone.

even the roads,
the poet says,
are mourning.

grief does that.
it gets into everything:
the path you used to walk,
the day of the week
you used to go.

it isn't foolish
to find it there.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “it isn't foolish to find it there.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
现在他们已经没有脚了。
没有歌声上山
在节日期间，
没有孩子在前面跑。

车轮车辙中的草。
温暖的石头上的蜥蜴。

就连道路，
诗人说，
正在哀悼。

悲伤就是这样做的。
它涉及一切：
你曾经走过的路，
星期几
你过去常去。

这并不愚蠢
在那里找到它。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 慢慢吸一口气，再读一遍最后一行：“在那里找到它并不愚蠢。”如果你带着这个真理，你会如何以不同的方式度过接下来的一个小时？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “通往锡安的道路哀伤，因为没有人来参加庄严的集会。”

paintings.title: is it nothing to you
paintings.epigraph: “Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by?”
paintings.poem:
the travelers keep walking.
they have their own errands,
their own long roads.

and the city calls after them
from the rubble:
is it nothing to you?

it's the oldest question
anyone in pain has asked.
does anyone see?

this whole book
is a hand on the sleeve
of whoever is passing.

stop a moment.
look.

some sorrow
only asks
to be seen.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “the travelers keep walking.” Looking through the lens of Lamentations 1:12, what does it mean to discover that “some sorrow only asks to be seen”?
paintings.zh_poem:
旅人继续前行。
他们有自己的使命，
他们自己的漫长道路。

城市在呼唤他们
从废墟中：
这对你来说没什么吗？

这是最古老的问题
任何痛苦的人都曾问过。
有人看到吗？

这整本书
一只手放在袖子上
无论谁经过。

停一下。
看。

一些悲伤
只问
被看到。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一个你体会过“旅人不断前行”的感觉的季节。透过耶利米哀歌 1 章 12 节的视角，我们会发现“有些悲伤只需要被人看见”，这意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “对你们这些路过的人来说，这没什么吗？”

paintings.title: open hands
paintings.epigraph: “Zion spreads out her hands. There is no one to comfort her.”
paintings.poem:
again and again
the chapter says it:
no one to comfort her.

so she does
the only thing left.
she spreads out her hands.

not a fist.
not a door slammed shut.
open palms,
empty,
held out into the air,

the way a child
holds up her arms
to be lifted.

an empty hand
is still a prayer.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the open threshold in this painting (Lamentations 1:17)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
一次又一次
本章说：
没有人安慰她。

所以她做到了
唯一剩下的东西。
她摊开双手。

不是拳头。
没有一扇门砰地关上。
张开手掌，
空,
举到空中，

像孩子一样
举起她的双臂
被解除。

空手
仍然是一个祈祷。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 仔细观察这幅画中敞开的门槛（耶利米哀歌 1:17）——如果你今天可以在它旁边留下一个令人焦虑的重物，你会放什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “锡安摊开双手。没有人安慰她。”

paintings.title: a cloud
paintings.epigraph: “How has the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger!”
paintings.poem:
the poet doesn't pretend.
he says it plainly:
a cloud came down
over the city
and the light went out of it,
and he names who he thinks
let it come.

the Bible lets him say it.
it doesn't cut the line
or tidy it up.

some grief is angry,
and aimed at heaven,
and heaven
keeps it in the book.

you can bring God
the hard sentence too.
he has heard it before.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the guiding cloud: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “some grief is angry, and aimed at heaven, and heaven keeps it in the book. he has heard it before”?
paintings.zh_poem:
诗人不假装。
他直白地说：
一朵云落下来
城市上空
然后光就从里面消失了，
他说出了他认为的人的名字
让它来吧。

圣经让他这么说。
它不会切断线路
或者整理一下。

有些悲伤是愤怒，
并瞄准天堂，
和天堂
把它记在书里。

你可以把上帝带来
难句也。
他以前听过。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让你的目光停留在引导云周围的笔触和光线上：当你读到“有悲愤，向天而去，天将其记在书中。他曾听过”时，你心中会升起怎样的安静祈祷？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “耶和华如何用云彩遮盖锡安的女儿呢？”

paintings.title: gates in the ground
paintings.epigraph: “Her gates have sunk into the ground. He has destroyed and broken her bars.”
paintings.poem:
gates were for keeping safe,
for closing at dusk,
for old men sitting in their shade.

now they lie half buried,
hinges in the dust,
the great bars broken.

nothing keeps anything out.
nothing keeps anything in.

some losses are like that.
the thing that held your life together
is lying in the dirt,

and all you can do
is sit beside it
and say so.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “gates in the ground” (Lamentations 2:9) from “gates were for keeping safe, for closing at dusk, for old men sitting in their shade” to “the thing that held your life together is lying in the dirt, and all you can do is sit beside it and say so”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
大门是为了保证安全，
黄昏时关闭，
适合坐在树荫下的老人。

现在它们半埋在地下，
灰尘中的铰链，
大铁条折断了。

没有什么可以阻挡任何东西。
没有什么可以容纳任何东西。

有些损失就是这样。
把你们的生活维系在一起的东西
躺在泥土里，

以及你能做的一切
坐在它旁边
并这么说。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 留心“地里的门”（耶利米哀歌 2:9）中的运动，从“门是为了保护安全，在黄昏时关闭，为坐在树荫下的老人”到“维系你生命的东西正躺在泥土里，你所能做的就是坐在它旁边这样说”——今天你发现自己在这条弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “她的大门已经沉入地下。他摧毁并折断了她的栅栏。”

paintings.title: they keep silence
paintings.epigraph: “The elders of the daughter of Zion sit on the ground. They keep silence.”
paintings.poem:
the old men sit down
on the bare ground
and say nothing.

dust on their heads.
rough cloth on their shoulders.

no speeches.
no answers.
they have lived long enough
to know
there aren't any yet.

if you are sitting
with someone in grief,
you may not need words.

sit down.
stay.

the ground is big enough
for two.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “they keep silence” (Lamentations 2:10) arrives at: “the ground is big enough for two.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
老人们坐下来
在光秃秃的地面上
并什么也不说。

他们头上的灰尘。
他们的肩膀上披着粗糙的布。

没有演讲。
没有答案。
他们已经活得够久了
知道
目前还没有。

如果你坐着
与悲伤的人一起，
你可能不需要言语。

坐下。
停留。

地面足够大
两个人。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 请注意“他们保持沉默”（耶利米哀歌 2:10）是如何演变为“地大得足以容纳两个人”。你生命中的哪些人今天正走在艰难的道路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “锡安女儿的长老们坐在地上。他们保持沉默。”

paintings.title: as big as the sea
paintings.epigraph: “For your breach is as big as the sea. Who can heal you?”
paintings.poem:
the poet searches
for something to compare it to,
something to say
that might help.

he tries one picture,
then another.

in the end
the only thing big enough
is the sea.

a wound as wide as the sea.
who can heal that?

he doesn't answer.
not yet.

but he kept reaching for words
because he wanted to comfort her.

that reaching
is already a kind of love.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of Lamentations 2:13: “that reaching is already a kind of love”?
paintings.zh_poem:
诗人寻找
来比较它的东西，
有话要说
这可能有帮助。

他尝试了一张照片，
然后是另一个。

最后
唯一足够大的东西
是海。

伤口如大海般宽阔。
谁能治愈它？

他没有回答。
还没有。

但他一直在寻找言语
因为他想安慰她。

那个达到
已经是一种爱了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今晚之前你记得的最重要的事情是哀歌 2 章 13 节中安静的教训：“到达就已经是一种爱”怎么办？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你的裂口大如大海。谁能医治你呢？”

paintings.title: pour out your heart
paintings.epigraph: “Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord.”
paintings.poem:
not a little.
not politely.
not only the parts
that sound like faith.

pour it out
the way you'd empty a jar,
upside down,
every last drop,
the grit at the bottom too.

get up in the night
and do it.

water poured on the ground
can't be gathered up again,

but it isn't lost.
it goes before the face
of the Lord.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the clay jar: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “it goes before the face of the Lord”?
paintings.zh_poem:
不是一点点。
不礼貌。
不仅仅是零件
这听起来像信仰。

倒出来
就像你倒空罐子的方式一样
颠倒，
每最后一滴，
底部的砂砾也一样。

半夜起床
并去做。

水倒在地上
无法再次聚集

但它并没有丢失。
它走在脸前
主的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下站在陶罐旁边的这个框架内：当你听到“它在主的面前”时，你一周中的什么匆忙或噪音开始消失？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “在主面前倾心如水。”

paintings.title: walled in
paintings.epigraph: “He has walled me about, so that I can’t go out.”
paintings.poem:
cut stone on every side.
paths that bend back
to where they started.

he calls out,
and it feels like the prayer
hits the ceiling.

this is the darkest room
in the whole book,
and it sits right in the middle.

it goes this low
before it turns.

if you are in the room
where the walls are close
and the prayers come back unopened,

keep reading.
the same voice
is about to say
something else.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “the same voice is about to say something else.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by Lamentations 3:7–9 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
在每一面切割石头。
向后弯曲的路径
到他们开始的地方。

他喊道，
感觉就像祈祷
触及天花板。

这是最暗的房间
在整本书中，
它位于正中间。

这么低
在它转动之前。

如果你在房间里
墙壁靠近的地方
祈祷文未打开就回来了，

继续阅读。
同一个声音
正要说
其他的东西。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在寂静中大声读出结束语：“同一个声音要说别的事情。”现在，《哀歌》3:7-9 给你心灵的哪一部分带来最深刻的审视或安慰？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他把我围起来，不让我出去。”

paintings.title: I forgot
paintings.epigraph: “Y ou have removed my soul far away from peace. I forgot prosperity.”
paintings.poem:
not just that things were bad.
he forgot
what good felt like.

the taste of an easy morning.
a table with enough.
a night of plain sleep.

that is the deepest part of grief,
when even the memory
of peace
goes quiet.

my strength has perished,
he says,
and my hope with it.

he writes that down honestly.

and then
he keeps writing.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Lamentations 3:17–18, grace meets us right beside the table set before you: how does the closing thought—“and then he keeps writing”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
不仅仅是事情很糟糕。
他忘记了
感觉多么好啊。

轻松的早晨的味道。
一桌就够了。
一夜安眠。

那是悲伤最深的部分
当连记忆
和平的
安静下来。

我的力量已经耗尽，
他说，
和我的希望。

他诚实地写下了这一点。

然后
他继续写作。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在耶利米哀歌 3 章 17-18 节中，恩典就在你面前的桌子旁边与我们相遇：最后的思想——“然后他继续写下来”——如何为你前面的道路奠定基础？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你让我的灵魂远离了平静。我忘记了繁荣。”

paintings.title: this I recall
paintings.epigraph: “This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope.”
paintings.poem:
nothing outside has changed.
the walls are still down.
the streets are still empty.

what changes
is what he chooses
to bring to mind.

he reaches into the ash
of everything he's lost
and finds
one coal still warm.

this I recall.

hope doesn't wait
for the ruins to be rebuilt.
sometimes it begins
with remembering on purpose.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “this I recall” (Lamentations 3:19–21) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“sometimes it begins with remembering on purpose”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
外面什么都没有改变。
墙壁仍然倒塌。
街道上仍然空无一人。

有什么变化
是他选择的
想起。

他把手伸进灰烬里
他失去的一切
并发现
一颗煤还热。

我记得这个。

希望不会等待
为了重建废墟。
有时它开始
有目的地记住。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天早上你走出的门旁挂着今天的“我想起这件事”（耶利米哀歌 3：19-21）的画，那么它的最后一行——“有时它是从刻意记住开始的”——会如何影响你的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我想起这一点，所以我有希望。”

paintings.title: new every morning
paintings.epigraph: “They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.”
paintings.poem:
yesterday's mercy
was enough for yesterday.

you don't have to ration it
through the dark.

every morning
the light comes up over the rubble,
and with it, kindness
enough for today,
fresh as the dew on the stones.

someone who had lost nearly everything
watched that sun come up
and said to God:
great is your faithfulness.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (Lamentations 3:22–23)—where in your own home or work today does “someone who had lost nearly everything watched that sun come up and said to God: great is your faithfulness” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
昨天的怜悯
昨天就够了。

你不必配给它
穿过黑暗。

每天早上
光芒照耀在瓦砾之上，
随之而来的是仁慈
今天就够了，
像石头上的露珠一样新鲜。

几乎失去一切的人
看着太阳升起
并对上帝说：
你的忠诚是伟大的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路历程中的每一站都展示了神如何在平凡的地方与我们相遇（耶利米哀歌 3：22-23）——今天，在你自己的家里或工作中，“一个几乎失去一切的人看着太阳升起，对神说：你的信实何其大”听起来是真实的吗？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “每天早上它们都是新的。你的忠诚是伟大的。”

paintings.title: my portion
paintings.epigraph: ““Yahweh is my portion,” says my soul. “Therefore I will hope in him.””
paintings.poem:
long ago, when the land was shared out,
every family got a portion:
a field, a vineyard,
a place to belong.

now the fields
belong to strangers.

and the poet looks around
at everything he no longer has,
and says:

the Lord
is my portion.

no one can carry that off.
no army
can march onto that field.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “no army can march onto that field.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
很久以前，当土地被分配时，
每个家庭都得到一份：
一块田地，一座葡萄园，
一个有归属感的地方。

现在田野
属于陌生人。

诗人环顾四周
他不再拥有的一切，
并说：

主
是我的份。

没有人能把它带走。
没有军队
可以进军那个领域。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 缓缓吸一口气，再读一遍最后一行：“没有军队可以踏上那片土地。”如果你带着这个真理，你会如何以不同的方式度过接下来的一个小时？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我的灵魂说：‘耶和华是我的产业，因此我要仰望他。’”

paintings.title: wait quietly
paintings.epigraph: “It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Yahweh.”
paintings.poem:
not pacing.
not fixing.
not running to the gate
every hour
to see who is coming.

just sitting
in the doorway,
facing east,
hoping.

it is good, he says,
to wait quietly.

quiet isn't giving up.
it's the stillness
of someone who believes
help is on the way.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “not pacing. not fixing.” Looking through the lens of Lamentations 3:25–26, what does it mean to discover that “it's the stillness of someone who believes help is on the way”?
paintings.zh_poem:
不踱步。
不修复。
没有跑到门口
每小时
看看谁来了。

只是坐着
在门口，
面朝东方，
希望。

这很好，他说，
静静地等待。

安静并不是放弃。
这是寂静
一个相信的人
帮助正在路上。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 回想一下某个赛季，您体会到“不节奏、不调整”的感觉。透过《耶利米哀歌》3:25-26 的视角来看，发现“这是一个相信援助即将到来的人的平静”意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “人应当盼望并安静等候耶和华的救恩，这是好事。”

paintings.title: not forever
paintings.epigraph: “For the Lord will not cast off forever.”
paintings.poem:
the grief is real.
the night is long.

but he does not
hurt us gladly,
and he will not
turn away forever.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the quiet centerpiece of “not forever” in this painting (Lamentations 3:31–33)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
悲伤是真实的。
夜很长。

但他不
高兴地伤害我们，
他不会
永远转身离开。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 仔细观察这幅画中安静的中心“不永远”（耶利米哀歌 3：31-33）——如果今天你可以在它旁边留下一个令人焦虑的重物，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “因为主必不永远丢弃。”

paintings.title: heart and hands
paintings.epigraph: “Let’s lift up our heart with our hands to God in the heavens.”
paintings.poem:
first, a searching.
let us look at our ways,
the poet says,
honestly,
and turn around.

then, a lifting.

not just the hands.
anyone can raise their hands.

the heart with them.

whatever is heavy in it,
whatever we have done,
whatever was done to us,

lifted up together,
the way you'd hold up
something broken
to someone
who knows how to mend it.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around your own two hands: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “whatever is heavy in it, whatever we have done, whatever was done to us, lifted up together, the way you'd hold up something broken to someone who knows how to mend it”?
paintings.zh_poem:
首先，进行搜索。
让我们看看我们的方式，
诗人说，
老实说，
然后转身。

然后，一个提升。

不仅仅是手。
任何人都可以举手。

心与他们同在。

无论里面有什么重物，
无论我们做了什么，
无论对我们做了什么，

一起举起，
你会坚持的方式
东西坏了
给某人
谁知道如何修复它。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 让你的眼睛停留在你两只手周围的笔触和光线上：当你读到“无论其中有什么沉重的东西，无论我们做了什么，无论对我们做了什么，一起举起，就像你将破碎的东西举起给知道如何修补它的人一样”时，你内心会升起什么样的安静的祈祷？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “让我们举起双手，仰望天上的上帝。”

paintings.title: until
paintings.epigraph: “until Yahweh looks down, and sees from heaven.”
paintings.poem:
his eyes won't stop.
no break, he says.
no pause.

and he isn't ashamed of it.
he tells us
how long he plans to cry:

until the Lord
looks down
and sees.

not until he's over it.
not until it makes sense.

until he is seen.

tears are not a failure of faith.
sometimes they are
how faith keeps watch.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Linger with the movement in “until” (Lamentations 3:49–50) from “his eyes won't stop” to “sometimes they are how faith keeps watch”—where do you find yourself along that arc today?
paintings.zh_poem:
他的眼睛不会停止。
没有休息，他说。
没有停顿。

他并不以此为耻。
他告诉我们
他打算哭多久：

直到主
低头看
并看到。

直到他结束为止。
直到它有意义为止。

直到看到他。

眼泪并不是信仰的失败。
有时他们是
信心如何守望。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 徘徊在“直到”（耶利米哀歌 3：49-50）中从“他的眼睛不停歇”到“有时它们是信心的守望”的运动中——今天你发现自己处于这条弧线的哪个位置？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “直等到耶和华从天上垂看。”

paintings.title: don't be afraid
paintings.epigraph: “Y ou came near in the day that I called on you. Y ou said, “Don’t be afraid.””
paintings.poem:
the lowest place.
water over his head.
a stone across the top.

I am cut off, he said.

and from down there,
where no one could see him,
he called on the Name.

here is what he remembers:
you came near.

not the rescue yet.
first,
a nearness.

and a voice in the dark
saying the thing
every frightened child
needs to hear:

don't be afraid.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Notice how “don't be afraid” (Lamentations 3:55–57) arrives at: “and a voice in the dark saying the thing every frightened child needs to hear: don't be afraid.” Who in your life is walking a hard stretch of road today and needs you to share this grace with them?
paintings.zh_poem:
最低的地方。
水漫过他的头。
上面有一块石头。

我被切断了，他说。

从那里，
没有人能看见他的地方，
他呼求圣名。

以下是他的记忆：
你走近了。

还没有救援。
首先，
一种亲近。

和黑暗中的声音
说那件事
每个受惊的孩子
需要听到：

别害怕。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 请注意“不要害怕”（耶利米哀歌 3：55-57）是如何产生的：“黑暗中有一个声音说着每个受惊的孩子都需要听到的话：不要害怕。”你生命中的哪些人今天正走在艰难的道路上，需要你与他们分享这份恩典？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我拜访你的那天，你走近了。你说，‘不要害怕。’”

paintings.title: stones in the street
paintings.epigraph: “The stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the head of every street.”
paintings.poem:
stones cut
for the house of God
now lie at street corners
where the carts go by.

it is hard to see
what you thought was forever
lying in the dust,

and harder
to walk past it
every day.

grief is like that.
it isn't one moment.
it's the corner
you have to pass
again tomorrow.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: What if the most important thing you remember before tonight is the quiet lesson of Lamentations 4:1: “it's the corner you have to pass again tomorrow”?
paintings.zh_poem:
石头切割
为了神的家
现在躺在街角
手推车经过的地方。

很难看到
你以为是永远的
躺在尘土里，

更难
走过它
每天。

悲伤就是这样。
这不是一瞬间的事情。
这是角落
你必须通过
明天再来。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今晚之前你记得的最重要的事情是《哀歌》4:1 中安静的教训：“这是你明天必须再次经过的角落”怎么办？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “圣所的石头倒在每条街道的尽头。”

paintings.title: clay jars
paintings.epigraph: “how they are esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!”
paintings.poem:
worth their weight in gold,
the poem says,

and now
treated like cheap clay jars,
the kind you use
and break
and toss on the heap.

that is what loss can do.
it tells you
you are common,
used up,
worth nothing.

but read the line again:
the work of the hands
of the potter.

even a clay jar
was made by someone
who shaped it
with care.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Imagine standing inside this frame beside the clay jar: what hurry or noise in your week begins to fade when you hear, “even a clay jar was made by someone who shaped it with care”?
paintings.zh_poem:
其价值相当于黄金，
这首诗说，

现在
像廉价的陶罐一样处理，
你用的那种
并打破
并扔到堆上。

这就是损失所能造成的后果。
它告诉你
你很普通，
用完，
一文不值。

但请再次阅读该行：
手的工作
陶工的。

甚至是一个陶罐
是由某人制作的
谁塑造了它
小心。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下，站在陶罐旁边的这个框架内：当您听到“即使是一个陶罐也是由精心塑造它的人制作的”时，您一周中的匆忙或噪音开始消失？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “它们多么被尊崇为陶罐，陶匠之手的作品！”

paintings.title: no one breaks it
paintings.epigraph: “The young children ask bread, and no one breaks it for them.”
paintings.poem:
of all the sorrows in this book,
this may be the smallest sentence
and the heaviest.

the children ask for bread,
and no one breaks it for them.

the poet doesn't look away,
and neither should we.

somewhere
a child is still asking.

bread is a small thing
to break.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Read the closing words aloud in the stillness: “bread is a small thing to break.” What part of your heart feels most searched or comforted by Lamentations 4:4 right now?
paintings.zh_poem:
这本书里所有的悲伤，
这可能是最小的句子
和最重的。

孩子们要面包，
没有人为他们打破它。

诗人没有移开视线，
我们也不应该。

某处
一个孩子还在问。

面包是一件小事
打破。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在寂静中大声朗读结束语：“面包是一件容易打破的小事。”现在，哀歌 4 章 4 节最能触动你内心的哪个部分？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “小孩子们要面包，却没有人为他们打破。”

paintings.title: the watchtower
paintings.epigraph: “In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save.”
paintings.poem:
every morning
up on the wall,
eyes on the far road,
watching for the help
they were counting on.

they watched
until their eyes failed.
the dust on the horizon
was only wind.

most of us have a tower like that:
a person,
a plan,
a rescue we keep watching for
that was never able to save.

it isn't wrong to hope.
it just matters
which way you are facing.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Lamentations 4:17, grace meets us right beside the stones of the wall: how does the closing thought—“it just matters which way you are facing”—steady your footing for the road ahead?
paintings.zh_poem:
每天早上
挂在墙上，
目光注视着远方的路，
寻求帮助
他们指望着。

他们看着
直到他们的眼睛失明。
地平线上的尘埃
只是风。

我们大多数人都有一座这样的塔：
一个人，
一个计划，
我们一直在关注的救援
那永远无法挽救。

希望并没有错。
这很重要
你面朝哪个方向。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《哀歌》4 章 17 节中，恩典就在城墙的石头旁与我们相遇：最后的思想——“你面向哪条路很重要”——如何为你在前面的道路上站稳脚跟？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “在我们的观察中，我们看到了一个无法拯救的国家。”

paintings.title: accomplished
paintings.epigraph: “The punishment of your iniquity is accomplished, daughter of Zion. He will no more carry you away into captivity.”
paintings.poem:
after all the dark
of this chapter,
one line of light
near the end:

accomplished.

the hard season
has an end.
no more carrying away.

you may not feel it yet.
the ruins still look like ruins.

but a word
has been spoken over them,

and the weight
you have carried so long
can be set down
in the grass.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If today’s painting of “accomplished” (Lamentations 4:22) hung beside the door you walk out of this morning, how would its final line—“but a word has been spoken over them, and the weight you have carried so long can be set down in the grass”—shape your choices?
paintings.zh_poem:
在所有的黑暗之后
本章的
一条光
接近尾声：

完成了。

艰难的季节
有一个结束。
不再带走。

你可能还没有感觉到。
废墟看起来仍然像废墟。

但一句话
已经对他们说过了，

和重量
你已经背负了这么久
可以设置
在草丛中。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果今天早上你走出的门旁挂着今天的“成就”（耶利米哀歌 4:22）的画，它的最后一行——“但对他们说了一句话，你长久以来所承受的重量可以放在草丛中”——会如何影响你的选择？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “锡安的女儿啊，对你罪孽的惩罚已经完成。他不会再把你掳去。”

paintings.title: remember
paintings.epigraph: “Remember, Y ahweh, what has come on us. Look, and see our reproach.”
paintings.poem:
our houses have other people in them now.
our fields
are someone else's harvest.

remember, Lord.

the last chapter
is a prayer
all the way through.

it doesn't begin with praise.
it begins with a list
of what was lost:
the house, the land,
the father at the table.

sometimes that's how prayer starts.
just telling God
what happened,
and asking him
to keep it in mind.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Every stop on the Pilgrim Walk shows how God meets us in ordinary places (Lamentations 5:1–3)—where in your own home or work today does “just telling God what happened, and asking him to keep it in mind” ring true?
paintings.zh_poem:
我们的房子里现在有其他人了。
我们的领域
都是别人的收获。

记住，主啊。

最后一章
是一个祈祷
一路过去。

它不是从赞美开始的。
它以一个列表开始
丢失的东西：
房子、土地、
父亲在桌边。

有时祷告就是这样开始的。
只是告诉上帝
发生了什么事，
并问他
记住它。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 天路历程中的每一站都展示了神如何在平常的地方与我们相遇（耶利米哀歌 5：1-3）——今天，在你自己的家里或工作中，“只要告诉神所发生的事情，并求他将这件事记在心里”听起来是真的吗？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “耶和华啊，求你记念我们所遭遇的事。看哪，看见我们所受的羞辱。”

paintings.title: water for money
paintings.epigraph: “We have drunken our water for money. Our wood is sold to us.”
paintings.poem:
water from our own wells.
wood from our own hills.

and now we pay for it.

it's the small things
grief takes
that surprise you:
a cup of water,
a fire lit
without counting sticks.

if even the simple parts
of your day
feel expensive now,

go gently.
it costs more
to live through a loss
than anyone can see.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Take a slow breath and read the final line again: “it costs more to live through a loss than anyone can see.” How would you walk through the next hour differently if you carried that truth with you?
paintings.zh_poem:
水来自我们自己的井。
我们自己山上的木材。

现在我们为此付出代价。

这是小事
悲伤需要
让你惊讶的是：
一杯水，
一把火点燃了
不用数木棍。

即使是简单的部分
你的一天
现在感觉贵了

轻轻地走。
花费更多
经历损失
比任何人都能看到的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 慢慢吸一口气，再读一遍最后一行：“承受损失的代价比任何人都想象的要高。”如果你带着这个真理，你会如何以不同的方式度过接下来的一个小时？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我们喝水是为了钱。我们的木材是卖给我们的。”

paintings.title: the lyre
paintings.epigraph: “Our dance is turned into mourning.”
paintings.poem:
no one at the gate
telling the old stories.
no young men
with their music.

the lyre lies in the dust.
the dancing stopped.

the poet doesn't hurry past it.

but there is another song
in Israel's prayer book
where the same words
turn the other way:
you have turned my mourning
into dancing.

the lyre isn't broken.
it's waiting.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Think of a season when you knew the feeling of “no one at the gate telling the old stories.” Looking through the lens of Lamentations 5:14–15, what does it mean to discover that “the lyre isn't broken. it's waiting”?
paintings.zh_poem:
门口没有人
讲述古老的故事。
没有年轻人
和他们的音乐。

七弦琴躺在尘土里。
舞蹈停止了。

诗人并不急于过去。

但还有另一首歌
在以色列的祈祷书中
哪里有相同的词
转向另一个方向：
你扭转了我的哀悼
跳舞。

竖琴没有坏。
它正在等待。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 想象一下某个季节，您体会到“门口没有人讲述旧故事”的感觉。透过耶利米哀歌 5 章 14-15 节的视角来看，发现“竖琴没有折断，而是在等待”意味着什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我们的舞蹈变成了哀悼。”

paintings.title: the fox
paintings.epigraph: “You, Yahweh, remain forever. Your throne is from generation to generation.”
paintings.poem:
the holy mountain,
where the songs went up,
where the crowds came in at festival,

a fox trots across it now,
nose down,
unbothered,
between the fallen stones.

that's how empty it is.

and in the very next breath
the poet looks up:

but you, Lord,
remain forever.

the mountain can be emptied.
the throne cannot.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look closely at the long climb up the hill in this painting (Lamentations 5:18–19)—if you could leave one anxious weight beside it today, what would you set down?
paintings.zh_poem:
圣山，
歌曲响起的地方，
节日期间人群涌入的地方，

现在一只狐狸小跑着穿过它，
鼻子朝下，
不受打扰,
掉落的石头之间。

就是这么空虚。

就在下一刻
诗人抬头一看：

但你，主啊，
永远保留。

山可空。
王位不能。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 仔细观察这幅画中漫长的爬山之路（耶利米哀歌 5：18-19）——如果今天你可以在它旁边留下一个令人焦虑的重物，你会放下什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “耶和华啊，你永远长存。你的宝座世世代代。”

paintings.title: renew our days
paintings.epigraph: “Renew our days as of old.”
paintings.poem:
the book ends
without tying it up.
its very last words
are still grief.

but just before them,
a prayer:
turn us back to you,
and we will be turned.
make our days new
like they used to be.

that is where it leaves you,
in the ruins,
praying.

not healed yet.
turned toward home.

and every morning
the mercy that is new
comes up again
over the broken walls.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Let your eyes rest on the brushwork and light around the stones of the wall: what quiet prayer rises in you when you read, “and every morning the mercy that is new comes up again over the broken walls”?
paintings.zh_poem:
书结束了
无需将其捆绑。
它的最后一句话
仍然悲伤。

但就在他们面前，
祈祷：
让我们回到你身边，
我们将会被转变。
让我们的日子焕然一新
就像他们以前一样。

那就是它留给你的地方，
在废墟中，
祈祷。

还没痊愈。
转身走向家。

和每个早晨
新的怜悯
再次出现
越过破碎的墙壁。

zh_beforeYouBegin:
《耶利米哀歌》是一本为倾倒之城流泪的书。耶路撒冷像寡妇一样孤零零地坐着。通往锡安的道路空无一人，城门已陷入地下，金色已黯淡，一只狐狸走过圣山。在这本书的中心，在黑暗中，一位诗人想起了一件事，并大声地说出来：他的怜悯每天早晨都是新的。你的忠诚是伟大的。

这本书用三十首短诗来贯穿它，分为五个部分，每一章对应古老的哀歌。每首诗都位于一幅画旁边和一行经文之下。这些照片保留了这座城市留下的东西——一盏低低燃烧的灯，灰烬中的余烬，一把躺在灰尘中的竖琴——并将面孔留给你的想象。如果你感到悲伤，这里欢迎你，不必急于走向充满希望的部分。

这些诗不是圣经。它们是一位读者对此的回应。打开这本书旁边的《耶利米哀歌》，让真实的话语成为最后的话语。
